title: weekday-pattern-heatmap-cluster-pool-2026-04-02
content:
Purpose:
This is a working export from the weekday-pattern heatmap dashboard for clusters and pools (daily aggregation) — intended for quick capacity planning and short-term scaling decisions. The export focuses on per-cluster / per-pool weekday utilization patterns (Mon–Sun) across the last 28 days, with annotations for recurring daily spikes and cross-region differences.

Summary (top-level findings):
- Overall fleet average utilization: 64% (28-day window).
- Clear weekday amplitude: Mon–Thu median ~72%, Fri dips to ~58%, weekends ~40–50% depending on region.
- Two clusters show chronic overcommit: cluster-gamma-eu and cluster-delta-na (pools: inference-prod, batch-rl); peak 95th percentile > 93% at 11:00–13:00 local time.
- Small pools used for experiments (pool-scratch-*) have sporadic bursts but low steady utilization; opportunity to consolidate into preemptible pools.

Export metadata / how generated:
- Dashboard: dashboards/gpu-weekday-heatmap-v2 (internal).
- Query used: SELECT date, cluster, pool, avg(util_percent) as avg_util, p50(token_latency_ms) as p50_lat, free_gpus FROM gpu_metrics.daily_grouped WHERE date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 28 DAY) GROUP BY date, cluster, pool;
- Aggregation: daily average util (0–100), P50 token latency (ms), free_gpus (count).
- Timezone normalization: each cluster normalized to its region local time before computing weekday buckets.

Patterns & interpretation (notes to self):
- Midday inference spikes (11:00–14:00 local) correlate with customer traffic windows; consider autoscale step-up at 10:30 and graceful step-down at 14:30 to reduce sustained burst pressure.
- cluster-gamma-eu / cluster-delta-na: sustained high util on training-batch and batch-rl pools. Options: (a) throttle lower-priority batch work to night windows; (b) move lower-priority jobs to dedicated reserved capacity for batch; (c) add 1–2 nodes to those clusters for short term.
- experiment-scratch pools represent ~7% of total allocated GPUs but provide <2% steady utilization — potential to reclaim and add to preemptible pool.
- FreeGPUs metric often zero at peaks — investigate whether autoscaler min replicas are too low.

Risks / caveats:
- Export uses daily averages; short sub-hour spikes (10–20 minute bursts) can be masked. Recommend follow-up with 5-minute bucket exports for flagged cluster/pool combos.
- Timezone normalization can hide region overlap issues for customers in multiple regions — double-check for cross-region routing rules.
- Maintenance windows and scheduled model rollouts can inflate weekday medians. Cross-check with maintenance calendar (linked).

Action items / next steps:
- [ ] Run 5-minute granularity export for cluster-gamma-eu and cluster-delta-na for last 7 days (assigned: Tom).
- [ ] Propose autoscaler policy change: add midday ramp policy for inference-prod pools (owner: Rajiv).
- [ ] Evaluate consolidation: move experiment-scratch* into a single preemptible pool and measure impact (owner: Lena).
- [ ] Add an alert for pool-level free_gpus <= 1 sustained for >30m (pager-worthy if customer SLA impacted).

Visual notes for SRE/Product handoff:
- Suggested viz: small-multiples heatmaps (by cluster) + rolling 7d sparkline per pool. Overlay annotation for scheduled rollouts.
- Color thresholds: <40% green, 40–70% amber, >70% red. For saturation alerts use >90% sustained 15m window.

Notes to reviewer:
- This is a working export intended for rapid iteration with SRE and product teams. It's purposely lightweight — followup exports should include 5m buckets and per-tenant breakdown for customer-facing clusters.

Historical context (why this matters):
- We saw a 14% QoS regression last July when a similar weekday spike pattern coincided with a large model rollout; proactive smoothing of midday spikes reduced 95th token latency by ~22% in that incident.
